reviews.reason: The numbered unit is structurally complete on printed p.121. Editorial approval remains withheld: the English resolves the initial giver, the grandfather phrase, and the final plural verb more confidently than the difficult printed syntax warrants. The recipient is not named here. A book is mentioned, but no wrapping or other physical presentation is specified.
reviews.suggested_text: Provisional only: “After this he gave me a sign concerning all the hidden things in a book, from my grandfather Enoch, and the parables that had been given to him; and they shall recount them to me in the account of the book of the parable.” The attachment of “from my grandfather Enoch” and the subject of “they shall recount” remain unresolved.
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain the lexical note on “parables,” anchored directly there. Replace the competing grandfather/“words of Enoch” explanations with one explicit syntax note; “words” should not be presented as an established reading of the grandfather expression. Explain that the asterisks belong to Charles’s printed editorial text, not to an uncontested manuscript transcription. Do not identify the narrator or giver beyond what this unit establishes.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Bounded repair: remove the unprinted ASCII apostrophe in ወእምድኅረ'ዝ, yielding ወእምድኅረዝ. Preserve the printed asterisks in *ትእምርተ and በ*ነገረ. No fully certified replacement transcription is supplied.

reviews.reason: The numbered unit is structurally complete on p.121, and Michael explicitly speaks to Raphael. The supplied judgment-word transcription ጽነኒ does not match the apparent printed ኵነኔ. The English also suppresses the difficult repeated ear-language and introduces judgment into an earlier clause as though its interpretation were settled. The concluding plural subject is not expressly identified.
reviews.suggested_text: Provisional only: “On that day Michael answered Raphael, saying, ‘The power of the spirit seizes me and stirs me to anger because of the terrible matter for the ear concerning hidden things [the ear-clause is difficult]. Who can endure the terrible judgment that has been carried out, before which they melt away?’”
reviews.footnote_changes: Place the textual-difficulty note at the ear/hidden-things clause, not at “answered.” Move “Or ‘drives me on’” to “seizes me,” rather than “executed.” Distinguish an interpretation involving judgment from the wording actually printed. Leave “they” unidentified. Treat melting as figurative language, not an instruction for bodily depiction.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Bounded correction indicated by the scan: ተገብረት፡ ጽነኒ → ተገብረት፡ ኵነኔ. Preserve the asterisks in ወ*ይእቲ and *ይመሥጠኒ. Approval of every remaining glyph is withheld.

reviews.reason: The numbered unit is structurally complete on p.121. Michael and Raphael are expressly named. The apparent printed judgment word is *ኵነኔ, not supplied *ጽነኒ. The closing sequence includes bracketed [እምኔሆሙ፡]; the current English silently smooths this editorially marked difficulty into a causal explanation and supplies “the sentence.” Its pronoun relationships are not secure.
reviews.suggested_text: Provisional only: “Michael answered again and said to Raphael, ‘Whose heart is not softened concerning it, and whose inward parts are not troubled by this word of judgment that has gone out against them [closing clause unresolved: “from them … who brought them out thus”]?’”
reviews.footnote_changes: Anchor the literal “kidneys” note to “inward parts,” not Raphael. Anchor the textual note to the closing clause. Remove the unsupported “from before them?” alternative and the unnecessary alternative that omits Michael. Explain the bracketed expression without treating it as an unqualified manuscript reading. Do not depict literal organ damage or assign identities to the closing pronouns.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Bounded repairs: *ጽነኒ → *ኵነኔ; ከመ'ዝ → ከመዝ. Preserve both the asterisk and [እምኔሆሙ፡] exactly as editorial features. The closing sequence remains on hold rather than being silently reconstructed.

reviews.reason: The numbered unit is structurally complete on p.121. Michael speaks to Raphael, and “Lord of Spirits” must be retained. The negative existence clause does not expressly name its subject: capitalized “He” supplies a personal referent, while advocacy or support is an interpretation, not an explicit noun. The opening standing subject and the objects of divine anger should not be identified more specifically from this unit alone.
reviews.suggested_text: Provisional only: “When he stood before the Lord of Spirits, Michael said this to Raphael: ‘It shall not be for them in the sight of the Lord, for the Lord of Spirits is angry with them, because they act like the Lord.’” The subject of “it shall not be” remains unresolved.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move the difficult-clause note directly to “It shall not be for them.” Present support or advocacy only as a possible interpretation, not the likely established meaning. Keep any alternative for the final comparison attached to that comparison. Delete the redundant “previous rendering” note. Do not turn the unclear clause into an assertion that God himself will be absent.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Bounded repair: ወከመ'ዝ → ወከመዝ. No conjectural subject, noun meaning advocacy, or additional divine title should be inserted into the source.

reviews.reason: The canonical source and English are structurally incomplete. The unit continues from p.121 onto p.122 through the second ለዓለመ፡ ዓለም።, before LXIX. The supplied expanded candidate reaches the correct boundary but is not an approved exact transcription: its እ-prefixed angel, human, and verb forms require correction against the printed negative ኢ forms. The internal sharing-verb glyphs also remain uncertified. Neither the referent of “them/they” nor an added complement such as “with them” is established explicitly.
reviews.suggested_text: Provisional whole-unit sense, not publication-ready: “For this reason all that is hidden shall come upon them for ever and ever. For neither angels nor a human being shall share a portion; they alone have received their judgment for ever and ever.” Retain a note on the attachment of the first eternity expression, the sharing clause, and the unresolved pronouns.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace the fragment-only notes with a cross-page coverage note and a textual note addressing the negative constructions and printed asterisks. Delete the duplicate previous-rendering note. Do not identify “them” as particular angels, humans, or another named group; do not add “with them,” “in it,” or a named punishment as though printed. Do not treat apparatus alternatives as the unanimous manuscript text.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Bounded repair instructions only: continue after the canonical final ለዓለመ፡ with the opening ዓለም፡ on p.122 and include the entire remaining unit before LXIX. Correct the candidate’s initial negative prefixes እመ… → ኢመ…, ወእብ… → ወኢብ…, and እ*ይት… → ኢ*ይት…. Preserve the printed asterisk on the judgment word and stop at ለዓለመ፡ ዓለም።. A complete exact replacement is withheld because the sharing-verb spelling and remaining continuation glyphs are not certified.
